title: Chicken and Rice Casserole
description: A creamy American-style chicken and rice casserole with tender chicken, vegetables, cheddar, and a golden baked finish.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt, plus more to taste
1/2 cup buttery cracker crumbs or panko
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Have the cooked chicken and rice ready before you start the sauce so the casserole can be assembled while the mixture is still warm.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until it becomes soft and translucent without taking on too much color.
Add the minced garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, then sprinkle the flour over the onions. Stir constantly for 1 minute so the raw flour taste cooks out and the mixture looks evenly coated.

Slowly whisk in the chicken broth, followed by the milk, adding each in a steady stream so the flour mixture stays smooth. Keep stirring until the sauce gently simmers and thickens enough to coat a spoon.

Stir in the thyme, salt, black pepper, peas and carrots, and 1 cup of the cheddar. Reduce the heat to low and stir just until the cheese melts; avoid a hard boil because dairy sauces can become grainy.

Add the cooked chicken and cooked rice to the skillet and fold gently until every portion is coated with sauce. If the mixture looks unusually dry, stir in a small splash of broth before transferring it to the baking dish.
Spread the mixture evenly in the prepared baking dish, pressing it lightly into the corners without compacting the rice. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar evenly over the surface.
Combine the cracker crumbs or panko with a teaspoon of melted butter if desired, then scatter the crumbs over the cheese to create a crisp topping that contrasts with the creamy casserole underneath.
Bake uncovered for 25–30 minutes, until the edges are bubbling and the center is piping hot. If you use a thermometer, the middle of the casserole should reach at least 165°F before serving.
Let the casserole rest for 8–10 minutes before spooning it out. The short rest helps the sauce settle around the rice, making the servings neater and reducing the chance of burning your mouth.
tips: Use cooked rice that is not overly soft so it keeps its texture during baking.
Rotisserie chicken works well and makes this a practical weeknight casserole.
Taste the sauce before adding the chicken and rice because the saltiness of broth and cheese varies.
commonMistakes: Using raw rice with this liquid ratio can leave the center undercooked.
Boiling the cheese sauce hard can make it grainy.
Skipping the resting time can make the casserole seem looser than it really is.
substitutions: Use cooked turkey instead of chicken.
Swap peas and carrots for broccoli or green beans.
Use Monterey Jack in place of part of the cheddar.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a covered container for 3–4 days.
Reheat covered until hot throughout, adding a splash of broth if the rice seems dry.
Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months and thaw overnight in the refrigerator.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Bacon Ranch Casserole
description: A creamy chicken bacon ranch pasta casserole with cheddar, tender chicken, smoky bacon, and a bubbly baked top.
ingredients: 8 slices bacon, cooked crisp and chopped
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil while you chop the cooked bacon and prepare the remaining ingredients.
Cook the rotini for about 2 minutes less than the package recommends for al dente pasta. Drain it well without rinsing, because slightly undercooked pasta finishes cooking in the sauce during baking.

Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, add the garlic, and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Sprinkle in the flour and cook for 1 minute while whisking so the sauce will not taste floury.
Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth, then simmer gently for 3–4 minutes until the sauce thickens. Reduce the heat and whisk in the softened cream cheese until no visible lumps remain.
Stir in the ranch seasoning, black pepper, 1 cup cheddar, and the mozzarella. Keep the heat low and stir only until the cheese is melted and the sauce looks smooth and creamy.

Add the drained pasta, shredded chicken, and about three-quarters of the cooked bacon to the sauce. Fold everything together until the pasta is evenly coated and the chicken is distributed throughout.

Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish and spread it into an even layer. Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar and the reserved bacon over the top so each serving gets a crisp, savory finish.

Bake uncovered for 20–25 minutes, until the edges are bubbling and the cheese on top is melted. If the casserole was assembled from chilled ingredients, allow a few extra minutes and check the center carefully.
Remove the casserole from the oven and let it rest for 5–8 minutes. Sprinkle with chopped chives just before serving so they stay fresh-looking and add a mild onion flavor.
Serve while hot, pairing it with a crisp salad or steamed vegetables to balance the rich sauce. Refrigerate leftovers promptly once the casserole has cooled enough to cover safely.
tips: Cook the pasta slightly under al dente so it does not become mushy in the oven.
Soften the cream cheese before adding it for a smoother sauce.
Reserve some bacon for the top so the final texture stays crisp.
commonMistakes: Overcooking the pasta before baking can make the casserole soft.
Adding cold cream cheese directly to hot milk can create lumps.
Using too much ranch seasoning can make the dish overly salty.
substitutions: Use penne or shells instead of rotini.
Use turkey bacon if preferred.
Swap some cheddar for Monterey Jack for a milder cheese flavor.
storage: Refrigerate for 3–4 days in a covered container.
Reheat covered at moderate heat so the sauce does not split.
Freeze portions for up to 2 months, though the pasta is best when freshly baked.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: BBQ Chicken
description: Juicy American barbecue chicken with smoky seasoning and a sticky, caramelized barbecue sauce glaze.
ingredients: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
instructions: Pat the chicken completely dry with paper towels, then place it on a tray. Dry skin browns more effectively and gives the barbecue sauce a better surface to cling to later in the cooking process.

Mix the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper in a small bowl. Rub the chicken with olive oil, then season every side evenly, including around the joints and underneath loose skin.
Prepare a grill for two-zone medium heat, aiming for roughly 375–400°F with one hotter side and one cooler side. Clean and oil the grates so the chicken is less likely to stick when it is turned.

Place the chicken skin-side down over the cooler side of the grill, close the lid, and cook for about 15 minutes. Turn the pieces and continue cooking with the lid closed so the interior cooks without burning the skin.

Combine 3/4 cup barbecue sauce with the vinegar and optional honey. Keep the remaining clean sauce separate for serving so no sauce that touches partly cooked chicken is used as a finishing condiment.

Move the chicken closer to direct heat once it is nearly cooked, then brush a thin layer of sauce over the top. Turn and brush again, allowing each coating to caramelize for 1–2 minutes before adding more.

Continue glazing and turning until the chicken is deeply browned and the thickest part reaches at least 165°F. For bone-in thighs and drumsticks, a slightly higher final temperature can make the meat more tender.

Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean platter and brush it with a final thin layer of the reserved clean barbecue sauce if you want a glossier finish. Never reuse the brush or sauce that touched raw chicken.
Rest the chicken for 5–10 minutes before serving so the juices redistribute through the meat. This rest also gives the sticky glaze time to set instead of sliding off immediately.
Serve with coleslaw, corn, baked beans, potato salad, or another barbecue side. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot throughout before eating.
tips: Use two-zone heat to prevent sugary barbecue sauce from burning.
Add the sauce near the end rather than at the beginning.
Use an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part without touching the bone.
commonMistakes: Saucing too early can burn the glaze before the chicken is cooked.
Cooking only over high direct heat often chars the outside too quickly.
Cross-contaminating reserved sauce with a raw-chicken brush is unsafe.
substitutions: Use boneless thighs and reduce the cooking time.
Use your favorite regional barbecue sauce style.
Bake at 400°F if grilling is not available, adding sauce during the final 10 minutes.
storage: Refrigerate for 3–4 days in a sealed container.
Reheat covered in the oven until hot, then uncover briefly to refresh the glaze.
Freeze cooked chicken for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Fried Steak
description: Southern-style chicken fried steak made with tenderized beef, a crisp seasoned crust, and creamy peppered country gravy.
ingredients: 4 beef cube steaks, about 5 oz each
1/2 tsp black pepper, plus more for gravy
instructions: Place the cube steaks between sheets of parchment or plastic wrap and gently pound any thick areas until the pieces are an even thickness. Pat them dry so the flour coating adheres instead of forming wet patches.
In a wide shallow dish, combine 1 cup flour with paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. In a second dish, whisk the egg, buttermilk, and optional hot sauce until completely blended.

Dredge each steak in the seasoned flour, dip it fully into the buttermilk mixture, then return it to the flour. Press the flour firmly onto both sides to build the craggy coating associated with chicken fried steak.
Set the coated steaks on a wire rack for 8–10 minutes before frying. This short rest hydrates the flour in spots and helps the crust stick to the beef instead of separating in the skillet.
Heat about 1/4 inch of neutral oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat until it reaches roughly 350°F. The oil should shimmer but should not smoke before the steaks are added.
Fry the steaks in batches without crowding the pan, cooking for about 3–4 minutes per side until the crust is deep golden brown. Transfer each finished steak to a clean wire rack to stay crisp.
Carefully pour off most of the frying oil, leaving about 3 tablespoons of browned drippings in the skillet. Lower the heat to medium, then whisk in the remaining 1/2 cup flour and cook for 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the milk, scraping up the browned bits from the skillet. Simmer gently for 4–6 minutes until the gravy thickens enough to coat a spoon, then season generously with black pepper and salt to taste.

Check that the beef is cooked to your preferred safe doneness and return the steaks briefly to a low oven if needed to keep them hot. Avoid simmering the steaks in the gravy or the crisp crust will soften quickly.
Serve each steak with warm country gravy spooned over the top at the last moment. Mashed potatoes, green beans, biscuits, or corn are traditional-style accompaniments for this hearty Southern meal.
tips: Rest the breaded steaks before frying so the coating adheres better.
Keep the oil near 350°F for a crisp crust.
Spoon gravy over the steak only when serving to preserve crunch.
commonMistakes: Crowding the skillet lowers oil temperature and makes the crust greasy.
Moving the steaks too soon can tear off the breading.
Adding milk too quickly to the roux can make the gravy lumpy.
substitutions: Use tenderized round steak if cube steak is unavailable.
Use regular milk mixed with a little lemon juice in place of buttermilk.
Use butter instead of pan drippings for the gravy.
storage: Refrigerate steak and gravy separately for up to 3 days.
Reheat steak on a rack in the oven and warm gravy gently on the stovetop.
Freezing is possible, but the fried crust is best fresh.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken and Dumplings
description: Classic Southern chicken and dumplings with tender chicken, vegetables, a creamy savory broth, and fluffy drop dumplings.
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery and cook for 7–8 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften without browning heavily.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then sprinkle 1/3 cup flour over the vegetables. Stir continuously for about 1 minute so the flour coats the vegetables and loses its raw taste.

Slowly pour in the chicken broth while stirring, scraping the bottom of the pot to dissolve any flour stuck there. Add the thyme and bay leaf, then bring the mixture to a gentle simmer rather than a rapid boil.

Simmer for about 10 minutes until the vegetables are nearly tender and the broth has thickened slightly. Stir in the shredded chicken, 1/2 cup milk, and frozen peas, then keep the pot at a gentle simmer.

For the dumplings, whisk the 2 cups flour, baking powder, and salt in a bowl. Stir in the 3/4 cup milk and melted butter just until a soft, shaggy dough forms; overmixing can make the dumplings dense.

Use a tablespoon or small scoop to drop portions of dumpling dough over the simmering stew, leaving a little space between them. Try to keep the portions similar in size so they finish cooking at the same time.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, because trapped steam is what cooks the tops of the dumplings and helps them rise.

After 15 minutes, uncover the pot and split one dumpling from the center to check doneness. It should look fluffy and cooked through with no wet flour in the middle; cook a few minutes longer if needed.
Remove the bay leaf, taste the broth, and adjust the salt and black pepper. If the stew is thicker than you prefer, stir in a small splash of warm broth without breaking up the cooked dumplings.

Serve immediately in wide bowls, spooning chicken, vegetables, broth, and dumplings into each portion. Cool leftovers promptly and store them covered, knowing that the dumplings will absorb more broth as they chill.
tips: Keep the stew at a gentle simmer so the dumplings cook evenly.
Do not lift the lid during the first 15 minutes of dumpling cooking.
Mix the dumpling dough only until combined.
commonMistakes: Boiling too hard can break the dumplings apart.
Overmixing the dough makes dumplings tough.
Adding too much flour to the stew can make it pasty.
substitutions: Use rotisserie chicken for convenience.
Use fresh parsley or chives in the dumpling dough.
Swap peas for green beans if preferred.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days in a covered container.
Reheat gently with a splash of broth because dumplings absorb liquid.
Freeze the chicken stew base for up to 2 months and make fresh dumplings after thawing for best texture.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Marsala
description: Italian-American chicken Marsala with golden chicken cutlets, mushrooms, and a savory Marsala wine pan sauce.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally to make four thinner cutlets, then pound any thick areas to an even thickness. Pat the cutlets dry and season both sides with salt and black pepper.

Place the flour in a shallow dish and dredge each cutlet lightly, shaking off the excess. A thin flour coating helps the chicken brown and later gives the Marsala sauce a little body without making it heavy.

Heat the olive oil with 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and sear for about 3 minutes per side until golden, working in batches if necessary.

Transfer the browned chicken to a clean plate. Add the sliced mushrooms to the same skillet and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their moisture evaporates and the edges begin to brown.
Add the shallot and cook for 2 minutes, then add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds. Keep the garlic pale because deeply browned garlic can make the delicate wine sauce taste bitter.

Carefully pour in the Marsala wine and scrape the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spoon to release the browned bits. Simmer for 2–3 minutes so the wine reduces slightly and the flavor concentrates.
Add the chicken broth and bring the sauce back to a gentle simmer. Cook for another 4–5 minutes until the liquid reduces enough to lightly coat the mushrooms and the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken and any juices from the plate to the skillet. Simmer for 3–5 minutes, turning once, until the cutlets are hot throughout and reach at least 165°F in the thickest part.

Turn off the heat and swirl in the remaining tablespoon of butter to give the sauce a glossy finish. Taste before adding more salt because the reduced broth and browned chicken already contribute seasoning.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with mashed potatoes, pasta, polenta, or green vegetables. Spoon the mushrooms and Marsala sauce over each cutlet just before the plates go to the table.
tips: Use dry Marsala wine rather than cooking wine for cleaner flavor.
Brown mushrooms well before adding liquid.
Thin cutlets cook quickly and stay tender.
commonMistakes: Crowding the pan steams the chicken instead of browning it.
Using sweet dessert Marsala can make the sauce overly sweet.
Reducing the sauce too far can make it salty.
substitutions: Use chicken thighs pounded to even thickness.
Use cremini or white button mushrooms.
If avoiding alcohol, use chicken broth with a small splash of sherry vinegar, understanding the flavor will differ.
storage: Refrigerate for 3–4 days in a covered container.
Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of broth.
Freezing is possible for up to 2 months, though mushrooms soften after thawing.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Piccata
description: Bright Italian-American chicken piccata with thin golden cutlets, lemon, capers, butter, and a light pan sauce.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally into thin cutlets and pound them to an even thickness of about 1/4 inch. Season both sides with salt and pepper so the quick-cooking pieces are seasoned all the way through.
Spread the flour in a shallow dish and dredge the chicken lightly on both sides. Shake off loose flour because a heavy coating can make the finished lemon-butter sauce cloudy and pasty.
Heat the olive oil with 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. When the butter foams, add the cutlets in a single layer without crowding the pan.
Cook the chicken for about 2–3 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer it to a clean plate as soon as the thickest part reaches 165°F, because thin cutlets can become dry very quickly.
Lower the heat to medium and add the optional wine or an equal amount of extra broth. Scrape the browned bits from the skillet and simmer for about 1 minute to concentrate the pan flavor.
Add the chicken broth, lemon juice, and capers and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2–3 minutes until it reduces slightly but remains loose enough to spoon over the chicken.

Return the chicken to the skillet and turn each cutlet once in the sauce. Warm for about 1 minute so the chicken picks up the lemon and caper flavor without spending enough time in the pan to overcook.
Remove the skillet from the heat and swirl in the remaining 2 tablespoons butter a little at a time. This off-heat step helps create a smooth, glossy sauce instead of an oily separation.
Taste the sauce and adjust with a small pinch of salt, more lemon juice, or a spoonful of broth if needed. Remember that capers are salty, so taste before adding extra salt.
Sprinkle with parsley and garnish with lemon slices. Serve immediately with pasta, rice, potatoes, or vegetables, spooning plenty of the warm lemon-caper sauce over each chicken cutlet.
tips: Pound cutlets evenly so they cook at the same speed.
Use fresh lemon juice for the cleanest flavor.
Whisk or swirl butter into the sauce off heat.
commonMistakes: Overcooking thin chicken cutlets makes them dry.
Using too much flour can thicken the sauce excessively.
Adding salt before tasting the capers can make the sauce too salty.
substitutions: Use extra chicken broth instead of wine.
Use chopped green olives if capers are unavailable, though the flavor will differ.
Use gluten-free flour suitable for dredging if needed.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of broth.
Freezing is possible, but the fresh lemon-butter sauce tastes best when newly made.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chicken Parmesan Casserole
description: A family-style chicken Parmesan casserole with pasta, marinara, tender chicken, mozzarella, Parmesan, and a crisp breadcrumb topping.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked diced or shredded chicken
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil while you measure the sauce, cheeses, chicken, and breadcrumb topping.
Cook the penne until it is about 2 minutes shy of al dente according to the package directions. Drain well without rinsing so the pasta keeps enough surface starch for the marinara to cling to it.

In a large bowl, combine the drained pasta, cooked chicken, marinara, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, 1 cup mozzarella, and 1/4 cup Parmesan. Fold gently until the pasta and chicken are evenly coated.
Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish and spread it into an even layer. Avoid pressing it down firmly, because a loosely packed casserole heats more evenly and is easier to serve.
Sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup mozzarella and 1/4 cup Parmesan over the top. Make sure the cheese reaches near the edges so every portion has a browned, cheesy surface.
Combine the panko with the olive oil and toss until the crumbs are lightly coated. Scatter the crumbs evenly over the cheese to mimic the crisp breaded element of classic chicken Parmesan.
Bake uncovered for 20–25 minutes, until the sauce bubbles around the edges and the center is fully hot. If the ingredients started cold, the casserole may need several extra minutes in the oven.
For a more deeply browned topping, broil for 1–2 minutes at the end while watching continuously. Breadcrumbs and Parmesan can go from golden to burnt quickly under direct broiler heat.
Remove the dish from the oven and let it rest for 8 minutes before serving. The rest allows the sauce and melted cheese to settle around the pasta instead of running immediately onto the plate.
Finish with chopped basil or parsley and serve with a green salad or roasted vegetables. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat until the middle is steaming hot before eating.
tips: Undercook the pasta slightly before baking.
Oil the panko so it browns evenly.
Use a marinara you enjoy because it provides most of the seasoning.
commonMistakes: Overcooked pasta becomes soft after baking.
Too much sauce can make the casserole soupy.
Broiling unattended can burn the breadcrumb topping.
substitutions: Use rotini or ziti instead of penne.
Use provolone for part of the mozzarella.
Use gluten-free pasta and breadcrumbs if needed.
storage: Refrigerate for 3–4 days.
Reheat covered, then uncover briefly to refresh the topping.
Freeze cooled portions for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken
description: Creamy Tuscan-style chicken with sun-dried tomatoes, spinach, garlic, Parmesan, and a rich skillet sauce.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper. If the breasts are very thick, pound them to an even thickness so the centers cook at the same rate.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for about 4–5 minutes per side until golden, then transfer it to a clean plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the butter. Stir in the garlic and sun-dried tomatoes and cook for about 1 minute, just until the garlic smells fragrant and the tomatoes begin to soften.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Simmer for 2–3 minutes so the broth reduces slightly and captures the flavor left from searing the chicken.
Lower the heat and add the heavy cream. Bring the sauce to a gentle simmer, stirring often, and avoid a hard boil because very high heat can cause the dairy to separate.
Add the Parmesan gradually while stirring until the cheese melts into the sauce. Continue simmering gently for another 2–3 minutes until the sauce lightly coats the back of a spoon.
Add the spinach in handfuls and stir until it wilts into the sauce. This should take only 1–2 minutes; keeping the spinach bright and just tender gives the finished dish better color and texture.
Return the chicken and any accumulated juices to the skillet. Simmer gently for 3–5 minutes until the chicken reaches at least 165°F and the sauce has thickened around the pieces.
Taste the sauce and adjust with black pepper or a small pinch of salt if needed. Sun-dried tomatoes and Parmesan are already salty, so seasoning at the end gives you more control.
Sprinkle with basil and serve immediately with pasta, rice, mashed potatoes, or crusty bread. Spoon the creamy tomato-spinach sauce over each chicken breast just before serving.
tips: Pound thick chicken breasts for even cooking.
Keep the cream sauce at a gentle simmer.
Add spinach near the end so it stays green.
commonMistakes: Boiling the cream aggressively can split the sauce.
Adding too much salt before the Parmesan can over-season the dish.
Overcooking chicken while thickening the sauce makes it dry.
substitutions: Use half-and-half for a lighter sauce, though it will be thinner.
Use boneless chicken thighs instead of breasts.
Use kale instead of spinach, allowing extra cooking time.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently over low heat and add a splash of broth if the sauce is too thick.
Freezing is possible, but cream sauces may change texture after thawing.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Marry Me Chicken
description: Modern American Marry Me Chicken with golden chicken, sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, herbs, and a creamy garlic pan sauce.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder. If any breast is much thicker than the others, gently pound it to an even thickness so all pieces finish together.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken without crowding the pan and sear for about 4–5 minutes per side until golden, then transfer it to a clean plate.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the butter, minced garlic, and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Stir for about 1 minute until the garlic is fragrant but still pale and the tomatoes soften slightly.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the skillet to release the browned bits. Simmer for 2–3 minutes so the broth reduces and carries the concentrated pan flavor into the sauce.
Add the heavy cream, oregano, and red pepper flakes and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Keep the heat moderate so the cream stays smooth instead of boiling rapidly and separating.
Stir in the Parmesan a little at a time until it melts into the sauce. Simmer gently for another 2–3 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Return the chicken and any juices on the plate to the skillet. Spoon sauce over the pieces and simmer gently for 3–5 minutes until the chicken reaches at least 165°F in the thickest part.
Taste the sauce before adding more salt because Parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes contribute plenty of savory flavor. Add a splash of broth if the sauce becomes thicker than you prefer.
Remove the pan from the heat and scatter fresh basil over the chicken. Let the dish stand for 2–3 minutes so the sauce settles and the basil releases its aroma without turning dark.
Serve with pasta, mashed potatoes, rice, or crusty bread to catch the sauce. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat gently so the cream sauce stays as smooth as possible.
tips: Use evenly sized chicken pieces for consistent cooking.
Add Parmesan gradually so it melts smoothly.
Fresh basil should be added after cooking for the best aroma.
commonMistakes: Overheating the cream can cause separation.
Cooking the chicken fully before returning it to the sauce can make it dry.
Salting heavily before Parmesan and sun-dried tomatoes are added can over-season the dish.
substitutions: Use boneless chicken thighs for a richer result.
Use half-and-half for a lighter sauce.
Replace red pepper flakes with a pinch of smoked paprika for less heat.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently over low heat with a splash of broth.
Freezing is possible but may slightly change the cream sauce texture.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
